test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If the manufacturer gains 10%, the wholesale gains 15% and the retailer gains 25%, then find the cost of production of a table (in ₹), whose retail price for the customer is ₹31,900. (NOTE: Manufacturer sells to wholesaler, wholesaler sells to retailer and retailer sells to customers.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **cost of production** be x.

Successive selling: x × (110 ÷ 100) × (115 ÷ 100) × (125 ÷ 100) = 31,900.

Using multiplier: x × 1.1 × 1.15 × 1.25 = 31,900.

x = 31,900 ÷ (1.1 × 1.15 × 1.25) ≈ 20,173.91.

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get 20,174.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20,174.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Retail Price** = ₹31,900, **Manufacturer Gain** = 10%, **Wholesaler Gain** = 15%, **Retailer Gain** = 25%.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100 | Production Cost = Final Price × [100 ÷ (100 + r₁)] × [100 ÷ (100 + r₂)] × [100 ÷ (100 + r₃)].
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb10dd7edf7c705adb96c7d6353924ab489b4b9f93d6f309a53264ce51e04596.png] 
⇒ Let Production Cost be P.
⇒ P × (110 ÷ 100) × (115 ÷ 100) × (125 ÷ 100) = 31,900.
⇒ P × (11 ÷ 10) × (23 ÷ 20) × (5 ÷ 4) = 31,900.
⇒ P × (1265 ÷ 800) = 31,900.
⇒ P = (31,900 × 800) ÷ 1,265.
⇒ P = 25,520,000 ÷ 1,265 ≈ 20,173.91.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20,174.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain of Profit

When a product passes through multiple hands, the final price is the result of **successive percentage increases** on the initial cost.

Successive Percentage Formula

Total Effective Gain % = [ (1 + r₁ ÷ 100)(1 + r₂ ÷ 100)(1 + r₃ ÷ 100) − 1 ] × 100.
